thread:
jamal: Heads-up — node gpu-34 just popped a bunch of Xid 63/32 entries and then dropped GPU from fleet. Pasting the key bits below. Can infra-telemetry help attribute faster?

sara: Thanks — can you paste the dmesg + journal snippet and the nvidia-smi at the time? Even a short window helps correlate.

jamal: Pasting ~30s around occurrence. don't need full dump.

jamal: ```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00:00): 63, PID=4321 0x1d4
[ 12345.679023] nvidia: GPU at 0000:65:00.0 has fallen off the bus.
[ 12345.680112] nv_peer_mem: unload_done()...
[ 12346.001233] device vfio-pci: remove, state 4
```

jamal: journalctl -u docker/containerd around that time showed OOM-ish churn but also kernel messages:```
Mar 15 12:01:23 gpu-34 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00:00): 32, PID=9876 0x6f
Mar 15 12:01:24 gpu-34 kernel: nvidia 0000:65:00.0: GPU hangs, schedule timeout.
```

jamal: and nvidia-smi output right after:```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| GPU  Name     Persistence-M| Bus-Id        | Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
| 0   A100-80GB       Off    | 0000:65:00.0 | Off    | 1                    |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Processes:                                                                  |
|  GPU   PID   Type   Process name                                         |
|  0     9876  C      /usr/bin/python3                                       |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

ops-bot: [alert] gpu-34 node-drain initiated (auto) — GPU ECC errors crossed threshold :warning:

akash: Looks like repeated volatile ECC + Xid 32/63. Could be flaky card or power/PCI issue. Do we have telemetry correlating node-level power rails or AMI kernel changes?

sara: We currently collect dmesg and journalctl for 5m around alerts and ship to the gpu-log-index. Parquet pipeline only keeps 30d. Two gaps: 1) we stop collecting when containerd restarts and 2) we don't parse Xid->hardware mapping reliably.

tk: Proposal: add a small log-harvester sidecar on low-cardinality nodes that streams only kernel/nvidia logs with line-level meta (node, PCI addr, boot_id, seq). We can then run quick heuristics: repeated Xid on same PCI -> mark as "card-level"; Xid across multiple GPUs on same power domain -> power/PSU suspect.

marie: For triage speed I'd like a one-line summary in the alert channel that surfaces: GPU, PCI, Xid code, recent process list, last successful health check, and a suggested next action (drain/replace/ignore). Could we compute that from current fields?

jamal: Yes — we can surface this when we parse these fields: Xid, ECC count, process pid+cmd, nv-host-engine logs. Example quick summary I want: `gpu-34 0000:65:00.0 Xid=63 ECC=1 topproc=9876(/usr/bin/python3) action=auto-drain`

sara: Implementation notes: existing parser is a python lambda that greps for "Xid" and emits raw lines. Need to: 1) associate journalctl boot_id with node boot, 2) normalize Xid codes (32/63/79 mapping to hang types), 3) enrich using nvml to map UUID->PCI if available, 4) attach recent nvidia-smi --query-gpu output.

tk: Quick grep helpers that saved time in previous incidents:```
journalctl -k --since '2026-03-15 12:00:00' -u kubelet | grep -E 'NVRM|Xid|nvidia' -n
# or dmesg slice:
dmesg --ctime --kernel | sed -n '12340,12360p' | grep -E 'Xid|GPU has fallen off'
```

akash: For machine learning teams: can we also capture a minimal stack-trace / process open files for the PID (if still alive) to help rule out bad tensor ops? Rough patch: sample `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` and `/proc/<pid>/fd` snapshot into the alert payload.

sara: Agree but privacy/PII concern — need to strip envs and only include binary path + open sockets. We'll make sampler opt-in for non-prod first.

marie: Operational flow: if parser sees >3 Xid events for same PCI in 1h -> auto-tag node for replace and open ticket assigned to hw-ops. If Xid events on different PCI but same host -> mark "power" and schedule a hardware check. WDYT?

tk: +1. Also include a decay window and suppress duplicate alerts for 24h once a hw-ops ticket exists.

jamal: One more ask — logs sometimes include encoded nv-host panic strings. Can parser base64-decode or at least include raw so we can paste into NV support.

sara: Good call. We'll preserve raw payload in an S3 blob and include a short-link in alert. Parser will emit schema: node, pci, xid_code, ecc_count, top_procs, nvidia-smi-snapshot, raw_blob_url.

ops-bot: [deploy] gpu-log-harvester v0.1 rolled out to 10% of GPU fleet for testing :rocket:

akash: Nice. For cost — make sure sampling window and retention are configurable per pool. High-throughput clusters might otherwise spike S3 costs.

sara: We'll add a quota and throttling layer. Initial rollout will target only GPU classes with ECC enabled and reduction sampling to 1min windows.

marie: Thanks all — will track on the incident ticket and loop in hw-ops if thresholds trigger. If anyone wants to help with parser tests ping me. :thumbsup:

jamal: I'll attach the full log blob to the ticket. Thanks for the quick responses.
